name: detached-triggers-controlled
whatItDemonstrates: Three detached triggers sharing one typed handle open a controlled alert dialog whose title text comes from each trigger's payload, with a plain button that opens it programmatically.
stateManaged: controlled — React.useState for open plus a second React.useState for triggerId; both are set inside onOpenChange (triggerId from eventDetails.trigger?.id) and by the programmatic button's onClick, then passed to Root as open and triggerId
nonTrivialInteractions: Triggers are rendered as siblings outside Root and linked to it via a shared handle from AlertDialog.createHandle<AlertPayload>(), with the same generic type argument mirrored on <AlertDialog.Root<AlertPayload>>

Each Trigger passes a distinct payload ({ message }); Root uses the function-as-a-child pattern ({({ payload }) => ...}) to render payload?.message as the Title text with an 'Are you sure?' fallback when payload is absent
onOpenChange receives (isOpen, eventDetails) and derives the active trigger from eventDetails.trigger?.id, feeding the controlled triggerId prop
A plain HTML <button> (not an AlertDialog part) opens the dialog programmatically by setting triggerId to 'alert-trigger-2' and open to true in onClick

name: detached-triggers-simple
whatItDemonstrates: A single trigger rendered outside AlertDialog.Root opens a simple discard-draft confirmation dialog through a shared handle created with AlertDialog.createHandle().
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state anywhere; open state is internal to Root and driven by the detached Trigger via the shared handle
nonTrivialInteractions: The Trigger is a sibling of Root (not nested inside it) and is linked to it by passing the same handle from a single AlertDialog.createHandle() call to both the Trigger's handle prop and Root's handle prop
Otherwise a minimal standard assembly: Portal, Backdrop, centered fixed Popup, Title and Description, and two AlertDialog.Close buttons (Cancel, Discard) as the dismissal affordances

name: hero
whatItDemonstrates: The canonical discard-draft confirmation alert dialog: an uncontrolled Root with a trigger, backdrop, centered popup containing title and description, and Cancel/Discard close buttons.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state; Root manages its own open state from the Trigger click
nonTrivialInteractions: Enter/exit transitions are styled via data-starting-style and data-ending-style attributes on both the Backdrop (opacity fade) and the Popup (scale plus opacity)
Dismissal is provided by two AlertDialog.Close buttons (Cancel, Discard) inside the popup; no Trigger-less or programmatic opening is involved

name: open-from-menu
whatItDemonstrates: A Menu item's onClick opens a controlled alert dialog, showing cross-component wiring between Menu and AlertDialog without any AlertDialog.Trigger.
stateManaged: controlled — React.useState boolean wrapping open, passed to Root's open prop; opened imperatively by a Menu.Item onClick that calls the setter, and closed via onOpenChange wired to the same setter
nonTrivialInteractions: The 'Delete…' Menu.Item uses onClick to set the React state that controls AlertDialog.Root's open prop — the alert dialog has no Trigger of its own
onOpenChange is wired directly to the same setState function so closes initiated inside the dialog (Close buttons, Esc) stay in sync with the controlled state
The Menu is fully assembled (Root, Trigger with caret icon, Portal, Positioner with sideOffset 8 and align start, Popup, Items, Separator) as the launching surface
